solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Grit discernible after emptying the sack (13)

indicatorNotes.emptying: an emptied word has lost everything between its outer letters, so only D and E remain

blocks.note: DiscerniblE emptied: just its outer letters
getting the sack is having your job terminated

annotation.surface: Squinting at gritty bits left behind after tipping out a sack.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes grit sand in a sack; the definition means strength of will. 'After' puts the emptied word before the sack.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: grit is courage and resolve, determination.

entries.clue: What might be under beachgoer’s dress on cold strand? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so DECK comes first

blocks.note: to deck out is to dress up
a strand of hair is a hair

annotation.surface: Wondering what a beachgoer wears underneath while standing on a chilly shore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strand' looks like the beach itself and 'dress' like clothing; both are wordplay. The 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a beachgoer sits on a deckchair, so it is literally under them.

entries.clue: Labour benefit after U-turn by right (7)

indicatorNotes.after: AVAIL comes after the turned piece
indicatorNotes.U-turn: a U-turn sends you back the way you came, so RT reads backwards

blocks.note: to avail is to benefit, as in 'of no avail'

annotation.surface: A welfare payment arriving after the government's policy reversal.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour, benefit and U-turn all point to politics; Labour here is just hard work.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: travail is painful toil, hard labour.

entries.clue: Point with meteor moving overhead, being miles away? (10)

indicatorNotes.overhead: in a down clue, the part overhead sits on top of the other

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, a point of land

annotation.surface: A stargazer on a headland watching a meteor cross the sky far away.
annotation.walkthrough: A ness is a point of land jutting into the sea, as in Sheerness and Dungeness.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition with a question mark: remoteness is the state of being far away.

entries.clue: Hotel capacity reportedly cut (6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so go by the sound

blocks.note: an inn is a hotel and its size is its capacity

annotation.surface: News that a hotel's number of rooms has been reduced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads like a report of a reduction, but it is the definition: to incise is to cut into.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to incise is to cut, especially to cut marks into a surface.

entries.clue: Bats entered Miami with the sun still rising (4,8)

indicatorNotes.Bats: bats means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: Bats flying into Miami just as the sun comes up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bats' opens the clue looking like animals; it is an adjective meaning crazy. Ante meridiem, a.m., is Latin for before noon.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: ante meridiem is the morning, while the sun is still climbing to its noon height.

entries.clue: Naughty child one year getting away with it (8)

blocks.note: a little imp is a mischievous child

annotation.surface: A naughty child who escaped punishment for a whole year.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: impunity is freedom from punishment.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by phrase: acting with impunity is getting away with it.

entries.clue: Ingenious rat’s inside opening trap (4)

indicatorNotes.inside: the inside of rat is its middle letter
indicatorNotes.opening: the A opens up the trap, splitting it to sit within

annotation.surface: A clever rat that has got inside and sprung open a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as a noun, a gap in the trap, but it is a verb: the A prises the net open.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a neat solution is an ingenious one.

entries.clue: Nick takes son on cycling tour, bonding time (9)

indicatorNotes.takes: the nick takes the rest inside it
indicatorNotes.cycling: cycling a word moves its first letter to the end, so TOUR becomes OURT
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, son placed on the tour comes after it

blocks.note: a chip is a nick, a small cut
TOUR with its T moved round to the end

annotation.surface: A father and son bonding on a bike tour.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'cycling' a bike ride; it is an instruction to rotate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: courtship is the period in which a couple forms a bond.

entries.clue: Minutes doubled for arrival, given directions mixed up (10)

indicatorNotes.doubled: the M in the arrival word is doubled by slipping another M in beside it
indicatorNotes.for: the pieces are given for the answer, followed by the directions

blocks.note: to be led is to be shown the way

annotation.surface: Minutes of a meeting twice recording an arrival, with the directions muddled.
annotation.walkthrough: Minutes suggests a meeting record; it is just M, added next to the M already in COMING.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: commingled means mixed together.

entries.clue: If not totally cloudy, perhaps removing top? (6)

indicatorNotes.removing top: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so S goes

blocks.note: a totally cloudy day is sunless

annotation.surface: A weather forecast hedging about a sky that is not quite overcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'If not totally cloudy' reads as one weather phrase; 'If not' is the definition and splits off.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: unless means if not.

entries.clue: Artillery not deployed in floods (12)

indicatorNotes.deployed: troops deployed are spread out in new positions, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Heavy guns kept back because the ground is flooded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not deployed' reads as one military phrase, but 'not' belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: raining torrentially is raining in floods.

entries.clue: Wire bent around a water pipe (5)

blocks.note: a hook is a wire bent round

annotation.surface: Bending wire round a pipe to fix it in place.
annotation.walkthrough: Hooka is a less common spelling of hookah. 'Around' belongs to the hook, not to the letters: it is not a container.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a hookah is a pipe that draws smoke through water.

entries.clue: Notice note inside car with large boot where deliveries are kept (5,8)

indicatorNotes.inside: the note goes inside the car word

blocks.note: an estate car is one with a big boot
n. is the abbreviation for note, as in footnotes

annotation.surface: A sign about a car whose big boot holds the parcels.
annotation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon. Poste restante is a post office service holding mail until collected.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: poste restante is the post office department that keeps letters for collection.

entries.clue: Burn black mass fetish (5)

blocks.note: to char is to burn black

annotation.surface: Something burnt at a black mass, a satanic rite.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black mass' reads as one phrase; 'black' goes with burn and 'mass' is just M.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a fetish is an object thought to have magic power, a charm.

entries.clue: Contents of cell unlikely to calm spy (9)

indicatorNotes.unlikely: an unlikely form of the words is an improbable rearrangement of them

annotation.surface: A prison cell holding an agitated spy who will not settle.
annotation.walkthrough: Cell makes you think of a prisoner; it is a biological cell.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: cytoplasm is the material inside a cell around the nucleus.

entries.clue: Bacon Clare unwrapped and put on beginning to sizzle (7)

indicatorNotes.unwrapped: unwrapping takes off the outside, so Clare loses its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to don is to put on

annotation.surface: A cook named Clare unwrapping bacon and putting it on to sizzle.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a kitchen scene, so 'put on' looks like cooking; it is DON, to put on clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: lardons are small strips or cubes of bacon.

entries.clue: Discipline is kept by decent soldiers heading for Troy (12)

indicatorNotes.is kept by: what is kept by something is held inside it, so IS goes in the word for decent
indicatorNotes.heading for: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the men are the rank-and-file soldiers

annotation.surface: Discipline held by honourable soldiers marching on Troy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heading for Troy' reads as a Greek army on the march; it just gives T.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: chastisement is punishment, discipline.

entries.clue: Musical mistakes all over the place in Kylie’s case (4,2,4)

indicatorNotes.all over the place: letters all over the place are scattered into a new order
indicatorNotes.case: a word's case is its outside, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A stage musical riddled with errors in Kylie Minogue's performance.
annotation.walkthrough: Kiss Me, Kate is the Cole Porter musical based on The Taming of the Shrew.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Cole Porter's 1948 Broadway show, a retelling of The Taming of the Shrew.

entries.clue: Not right, like factory without power (6)

indicatorNotes.without: without power means the P is left out

blocks.note: PLANT, a factory, minus P for power

annotation.surface: A factory that has lost its power and is not working properly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not right' sounds like 'wrong'; here right means upright, and aslant means tilted.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: aslant means at a slant, not upright.

entries.clue: Swede in US first grades range on dull course (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, pieces put on another come after it

blocks.note: a rut is a dull routine
A and B are the top grades
an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

annotation.surface: A Swedish student in America getting top marks across a boring course.
annotation.walkthrough: Swede is the vegetable, not a person from Sweden; Americans call it rutabaga.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional synonym: swede is the British word for the root Americans call rutabaga.

entries.clue: Scientist such as Linnaeus not a bit confused about origin of species? (8)

indicatorNotes.about: the jumbled letters go about, around, the S
indicatorNotes.origin of: a word's origin is its first letter

annotation.surface: The great naturalist Linnaeus perfectly clear about Darwin's Origin of Species.
annotation.walkthrough: The Origin of Species is Darwin's book, which Linnaeus predated; here origin just means first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Linnaeus, who classified plants, was a botanist.

entries.clue: Racehorses unlikely to change (6)

blocks.note: a trainer's whole string of horses, named after the building that houses them

annotation.surface: Racehorses set in their ways.
annotation.walkthrough: A stable is both the building and the collection of horses a trainer keeps.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a stable of racehorses, and stable meaning steady.

entries.clue: Spot evil guards have no explosive (9)

indicatorNotes.guards: to guard is to surround, so evil holds the rest inside

blocks.note: to lack is to have no

annotation.surface: Villains guarding a spot with no explosives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a place to guard; it is a pimple.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a blackhead is a kind of spot on the skin.

entries.clue: Weakness of swan song (8)

blocks.note: a pen is a female swan

annotation.surface: The frailty of a dying swan's final song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swan song' reads as one phrase, a final performance; split it into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a weakness for something is a penchant, a liking.

entries.clue: Merchandise prepared by Spooner’s impossible to shift (4-6)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: merchandise is stock; it hands over its ST and takes the R from the next word
prepared is ready; it gives up its R and takes the ST in exchange

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper's goods prepared and too heavy to move.
annotation.walkthrough: The spoonerism swaps whole opening clusters: ST-ock R-eady becomes R-ock ST-eady.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something rock-steady is too firm to move.

entries.clue: Gemstone queen brought in taxi to pawnbroker (9)

indicatorNotes.brought in: the queen is brought into the taxi
indicatorNotes.to: the pawnbroker is added to it

blocks.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

annotation.surface: A queen taking a cab to pawn her jewel.
annotation.walkthrough: A carbuncle is a red garnet cut into a rounded shape.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a carbuncle is a red gemstone.

entries.clue: Very different pictures on pavement, say around drain (7,5)

indicatorNotes.around: the pictures go around the drain

blocks.note: chalk pictures on pavements are street art
to sap is to drain strength

annotation.surface: Chalk drawings on a pavement around a drain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks pavement pictures as one example of street art.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: two places many streets from each other are far apart, and figuratively that distance means unlike.

entries.clue: Series of routs with English involved, giving away runs (3,5)

indicatorNotes.involved: English is involved, wrapped in the routs word
indicatorNotes.giving away: to give away runs is to lose them, so R goes

blocks.note: R, the cricket abbreviation for runs, is removed

annotation.surface: A cricket series of English humiliations, with runs thrown away.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket Test series between England and Australia, so the whole surface is cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the Ashes is a cricket Test series.

entries.clue: Romeo wears young ladies’ underwear (8)

indicatorNotes.wears: what is worn is covered, so Romeo is worn by the young ladies

blocks.note: fillies is slang for young women

annotation.surface: A Romeo who puts on young women's underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts Romeo in the underwear; it is the young ladies who wear him.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: frillies are frilly women's underwear.

entries.clue: Group rounded up, picked up when caught (4)

indicatorNotes.picked up: what is picked up by ear is heard, so go by the sound

blocks.note: to catch a remark is to hear it

annotation.surface: A gang of suspects rounded up and caught.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' and 'caught' both read as arrests; one is the sound signal and the other is heard.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a herd is a group of animals rounded up together.

entries.clue: Composer Harry has almost no debt to speak of (6,7)

indicatorNotes.to speak of: spoken, so go by the sound

blocks.note: to harry is to hector, to bully
someone with almost no debt barely owes

annotation.surface: A composer named Harry who is nearly out of debt.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a first name to match the composer's; it is a verb, and Hector is the name that answers it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer.

entries.clue: Second chance for students almost free from drugs gang (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the word means all but its last letter

blocks.note: CLEAN, off drugs, minus its last letter
a ring is a criminal gang

annotation.surface: Students nearly off drugs but back with a gang.
annotation.walkthrough: Clearing is the UK university process that matches students who missed their offers to spare places.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: clearing gives students without a place a second chance at university.

entries.clue: Anti-aircraft cannon of era, like one always striking tails (8)

indicatorNotes.always striking tails: striking off tails removes last letters, and always means from every word

annotation.surface: An old gun that always hits aircraft from behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tails' makes you picture aircraft tails; it means last letters of words. The Oerlikon was a Swiss 20mm gun of the Second World War.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a Swiss-designed 20mm gun used against aircraft in the Second World War.

entries.clue: Record incident with eyes peeled, in a sense (7-5)

indicatorNotes.peeled: a peeled word loses its outer letters, so EYES becomes YE
indicatorNotes.in: the pieces go in the sense

blocks.note: sight is one of the five senses

annotation.surface: Keeping your eyes peeled to note an incident.
annotation.walkthrough: A seventy-eight is an old gramophone record that played at 78 rpm. 'Eyes peeled' is an idiom for watchful here turned literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a seventy-eight is a shellac record.

entries.clue: Take game when returning set of crockery after separation (5,7)

indicatorNotes.after: the crockery comes after the separation

blocks.note: a dinner service is a set of crockery

annotation.surface: Divorcing couple returning the dinner set after they split up.
annotation.walkthrough: In tennis the returner wins a game against the server by breaking service. 'Returning' reads as giving back crockery.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: to break service is to win a game while receiving.

entries.clue: Reason Yankee crosses Washington Bridge? (8)

indicatorNotes.crosses: Yankee crosses to the far side of Washington, landing after WA

annotation.surface: Wondering why a Yankee crosses the George Washington Bridge.
annotation.walkthrough: Washington Bridge reads as a single landmark; the question mark says a causeway is only a sort of bridge.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition with a question mark: a causeway is a raised road over water, much like a bridge.

entries.clue: A leisurely walk back collecting small bits and bobs (3-5)

indicatorNotes.back: sent back, the walk reads in reverse
indicatorNotes.collecting: the reversed walk collects S inside it

blocks.note: a stroll is a leisurely walk

annotation.surface: A slow walk home picking up odds and ends.
annotation.walkthrough: Allsorts is best known from Liquorice Allsorts, a British sweet mix of assorted pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: allsorts are an assortment, bits and bobs.

entries.clue: Now what follows 29 across in list of four-letter words? (4)

indicatorNotes.what follows: the word that comes next in an alphabetical list

blocks.clueFragment: what follows 29 across in list of four-letter words
blocks.note: the next four-letter word after the 29 across answer in an alphabetical list

annotation.walkthrough: Swap HERD's last letter for the next one in the alphabet. Here means now, as in 'here we go'.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: here can mean at this point in time, now.

entries.clue: Old-fashioned romance, type with ladies or gents separated by screen (4,4,2)

indicatorNotes.separated by: the ladies or gents are split apart and the screen sits in the gap

blocks.note: a make is a type or brand
the Ladies and the Gents are British names for public toilets, loos

annotation.surface: A period romance of a type where men and women are kept apart by a screen.
annotation.walkthrough: In older English 'make love to' meant to court or woo, not to have sex; the definition says so.
annotation.definitionFit: Dated sense: to make love to someone once meant to court them, to romance them.
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a noun phrase, the answer a verb phrase meaning to romance

entries.clue: Granny’s getting into airline stock which may lead to downfall (6,4)

indicatorNotes.getting into: Granny's gets into the airline and stock, between them

blocks.note: nana is granny, and the 's carries over

annotation.surface: A granny investing in airline shares that could ruin her.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stock' reads as shares; it is family line. A banana skin is British for a trap that trips up a politician.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative definition: a banana skin is a slip that leads to someone's fall.

entries.clue: ROH etc somehow accommodating band with one? (9,3)

annotation.definition: ROH etc somehow accommodating band with one?

indicatorNotes.somehow: somehow means in some rearranged way
indicatorNotes.accommodating: the rearranged letters accommodate the band and one inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder; ROH is the Royal Opera House

annotation.surface: Opera houses making room for their musicians.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: places like the Royal Opera House have one of these to hold the band.
annotation.definitionFit: &lit: an opera house has an orchestra pit to accommodate its band.

entries.clue: Keeper who tends to shoot? (4,6)

blocks.note: the surface suggests a goalkeeper; it is someone who keeps animals
the surface means inclined to shoot; the setter means looking after the game that is shot

annotation.surface: A goalkeeper who likes to have a shot at goal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tends to' reads as 'is inclined to'; it means 'tends' as in looks after, and the game is what shooting parties shoot.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a game warden tends game animals.

entries.clue: Thing developing thirst in From Dusk Till Dawn? (9)

indicatorNotes.developing: a developing thing changes its form, so the letters rearrange

blocks.note: to thirst for something is to long for it

annotation.surface: A creature growing thirsty in the vampire film From Dusk Till Dawn.
annotation.walkthrough: From Dusk Till Dawn is a vampire film, hence the thirst; the question mark makes the title the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: nightlong means lasting from dusk until dawn.

entries.clue: Sweetener lifted an uncommonly good medicine (8)

indicatorNotes.lifted: in a down clue, lifting the pieces makes them read upwards

blocks.note: rare means uncommonly good, as in a rare talent

annotation.surface: A spoonful of sugar lifting an unusually good medicine.
annotation.walkthrough: A nod to 'a spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down'. Demerara is a brown cane sugar.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: demerara is a sugar, a sweetener.

entries.clue: Half a pair of pants? (6)

blocks.note: the surface suggests trousers; the setter means gasps, as in pants and puffs
a pant is one gasp for air, so a pair of them is two gasps

annotation.surface: One leg of a pair of trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: A pair of pants is trousers (or, in Britain, underwear), which have no halves worth naming; pants as gasps do.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: one pant is a breath, half a pair of pants.

entries.clue: Some vessels went back with nothing to report (8)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the words gives a run of their letters
indicatorNotes.went back: going back means reading right to left

blocks.note: read right to left through veSSELS WENt

annotation.surface: Ships returning from a voyage with no news.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Went back' reads as the ships sailing home; it is an instruction to read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: newsless means having no news to tell.

entries.clue: Cockchafer could be a pest (3,3)

annotation.surface: A beetle said to be a garden pest.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plain statement about the beetle; the wordplay splits it after the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the cockchafer is also called the maybug.

entries.clue: Drinking session includes large mixer (7)

indicatorNotes.includes: the drinking session includes L inside it

blocks.note: a bender is a drinking spree

annotation.surface: A night of drinking with plenty of tonic and soda.
annotation.walkthrough: Mixer suggests something added to spirits; here it is a kitchen blender.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a blender is a food mixer.

entries.clue: Bones in area behind grave (6)

indicatorNotes.behind: in a down clue the area comes behind, below, the grave

annotation.surface: Bones found in the area behind a grave.
annotation.walkthrough: Grave is an adjective here, not a burial place. Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: sterna are breastbones.

entries.clue: Upset secretary rings to ask about dismissal (6)

indicatorNotes.Upset: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads upwards

annotation.surface: An upset secretary phoning to ask about being sacked.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders appeal to the umpire to give a batsman out, so the dismissal is a batsman's, not the secretary's.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: in cricket to appeal is to ask the umpire whether a batsman is out.

entries.clue: Diversion connected with funeral activity ruling motorway out (10)

indicatorNotes.out: with ruling, it takes the M out

blocks.note: cremation takes place at some funerals
M, the British motorway prefix as in M1, is removed

annotation.surface: A road diversion near a funeral, keeping traffic off the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: Diversion reads as a road detour next to motorway; it means a pastime.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a diversion is an amusement, a recreation.

entries.clue: While driving, come across butcher (3,2)

blocks.note: to cut someone up is to pull in sharply in front of them

annotation.surface: A driver who happens upon a butcher's shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come across' reads as happen upon; it means swerve across another car's path.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to cut up another driver, and to cut up meat like a butcher.

entries.clue: Second in line relation taking charge after this guy? (4,8)

annotation.definition2: relation taking charge after this guy?

blocks.note: next after the monarch in succession

blocks.clueFragment: relation taking charge after this guy?
blocks.note: a relative who will take over when the current ruler goes

annotation.surface: A family member waiting to take over once the boss has gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second in line' could be a queue; in royalty it is the one after the reigning monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Two descriptions of the heir apparent, who is next in line and will succeed the current holder.

entries.clue: Eg PB concealed by slowest athlete? (4)

indicatorNotes.concealed by: the answer is concealed by the words, in their letters

annotation.surface: A slow runner hiding a personal best.
annotation.walkthrough: PB is a personal best, a statistic an athlete records.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a PB is one kind of stat.

entries.clue: Three is one and two and zero (7)

annotation.definition: Three is one and two and zero

blocks.note: the surface suggests a sum or a riddle; read it as naming three as one example of a kind of number
two and zero are further examples of the same kind

annotation.surface: A puzzling sum claiming three equals one plus two plus zero.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as arithmetic, but it is a list: three, two and zero are each an integer.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: three, two and zero are all whole numbers, integers.

entries.clue: Ship out of jurisdiction added E in Morse and en clair (9)

blocks.note: E in Morse code is a single dot, spoken as dit
en clair means in plain text, so E in plain text is just E

annotation.surface: A coded message about a deportation, with an extra E in Morse and in plain text.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' joins two versions of E: the dit of Morse, then the letter in plain language.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: to extradite is to send someone out of a jurisdiction to face trial.

entries.clue: Nice fellow always forgetting name for my boy (5)

indicatorNotes.always forgetting: forgetting leaves out, and always means in each word

blocks.note: a don is a university fellow
N, standard abbreviation, dropped from each word

annotation.surface: A kind man who keeps forgetting his son's name.
annotation.walkthrough: Nice at the start of the clue could be the French city; here it is kind. Kiddo is a familiar name for a child.
annotation.definitionFit: Familiar synonym: kiddo is an affectionate term like my boy.

entries.clue: Spanish dance with fire at a tea party (9)

blocks.note: to zap is to fire at

annotation.surface: A Spanish dance performed with fiery passion at a tea party.
annotation.walkthrough: A zapateado is a flamenco dance with rapid heel stamping. 'A tea party' reads as one event; party gives DO.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a flamenco-style dance from Spain built on rapid stamping of the heels.

entries.clue: Blanket becoming frayed in gardener’s basket (10,3)

indicatorNotes.in: the fraying word goes in the basket

blocks.note: a trug is a shallow wooden garden basket
fabric that ravels comes apart in threads

annotation.surface: A blanket fraying in a garden basket.
annotation.walkthrough: Ravel usually means tangle but can also mean fray. A travelling rug is a blanket to keep your legs warm on a journey.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a thick rug for wrapping round your legs on a journey, one sort of blanket.
